alta-dighi-national-park.desc: Alta Dighi is a long, deep tank of about 43 acres, roughly 1.1 km long and 500 m wide, with high banks and sal forest on its southern side. The forest around it, about 264 hectares, was declared a national park in 2011. It is one of the largest old tanks still holding water in the country, older than Ramsagar, and a local story says the king dug it as far as his mother could walk. Winter brings migratory birds, and the forest paths are quiet and shady.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus from Naogaon to Dhamoirhat, then a CNG or auto-rickshaw to Alta Dighi.
Good to know
The tank lies right by the Indian border; stay away from the border line and follow BGB instructions.

kusumba-mosque.desc: Built in 1558–59 during the late Sultanate period, Kusumba Mosque is unusual in Bengal for its outer facing of dark stone over a brick core. It has six domes in two rows and fine carving on its mihrabs, including a raised platform inside. The mosque overlooks a wide pond, and the reflection of its sober facade in the water is memorable. It remains in use for daily prayers.
blocks: How to get there
In Manda upazila, about 35 km from Naogaon town; take a bus towards Manda and get off at Kusumba.
Good to know
Dress modestly and avoid prayer times. Combine with a drive across the Barind countryside.

jagaddala-mahavihara.desc: Jagaddala was a Buddhist monastery thought to have been founded under King Ramapala in the late 11th century, and it was known as a centre of scholarship. The excavated site in Dhamoirhat upazila shows brick walls, cells and structural remains in a quiet rural setting near the border. It sees only a fraction of Paharpur's visitors. For those interested in Bengal's Buddhist past it completes the story.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus to Dhamoirhat from Naogaon town, then a local auto-rickshaw to Jagaddal village.
Good to know
Facilities are minimal; carry water. It is near the border, so carry ID.

dibar-dighi.desc: Dibar Dighi lies in Dibar village in Patnitala upazila, beside the Najipur–Sapahar road. In the middle of the tank stands a tall, uninscribed granite pillar with a crown-like top ringed by three bands, its lower part under water. Historians link it to Divya (Dibyak), the Kaivarta chief who rebelled against the Pala king Mahipala II in the 11th century and took over Varendra, and the village name may come from him. Local legend prefers a simpler story: that a jinn dug the tank in a single night.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus from Naogaon to Najipur (Patnitala), then a CNG or auto-rickshaw along the Sapahar road to Dibar.
Good to know
The water level changes how much of the pillar you see; it shows best in the dry season. Combine with Alta Dighi on the same day.

dubalhati-rajbari.desc: Dubalhati Rajbari stands about 7 km south-west of Naogaon town. The Dubalhati rajas held land as far away as Sylhet, Dinajpur, Rangpur and parts of India, and built a huge two-storey palace here with rows of Roman-style pillars, ponds on four sides, temples and a school. The estate grew most under Raja Harnath Roy Chowdhury, and the Raja Harnath High School, founded in 1864, is still running. Today much of the palace is roofless and overgrown, but its scale is still impressive.
blocks: How to get there
Take an auto-rickshaw or CNG from Naogaon town; it takes about 20–30 minutes.
Good to know
The ruins are fragile; do not climb on walls or go into unsafe rooms.

patisar-kuthibari.desc: Patisar was the seat of the Tagore family's Kaligram estate, and Rabindranath stayed here on visits as zamindar. He took a keen interest in rural welfare, setting up a school and an agricultural bank for local farmers. The two-storey kuthibari now displays furniture, photographs and objects linked to his stays. The quiet riverside village still has the rural feel he wrote about.
blocks: How to get there
From Atrai in southern Naogaon (reachable by train), take a CNG or auto-rickshaw about 12 km to Patisar.
Good to know
Check opening days locally. The Tagore birthday celebrations in early May are lively.

patisar-rabindra-jayanti.desc: Every year on 25 Boishakh, Rabindranath Tagore's birth anniversary, Patisar hosts celebrations around the kuthibari. Local and visiting artists perform Rabindra Sangeet, recite poetry and stage short plays, and a fair springs up with food and craft stalls. Villagers who remember the zamindar's school and bank in family stories take part with pride. It is a warm, small-scale way to experience Tagore's place in Bangladeshi culture.
blocks: How to get there
As for Patisar Kuthibari: via Atrai, then by CNG.
Good to know
It is hot in May; go early in the day and carry water.

somapura-mahavihara.desc: Founded under the Pala king Dharmapala in the late 8th century, Somapura Mahavihara was a major centre of Buddhist learning for centuries. Today you can walk around a huge square courtyard lined with the remains of monks' cells, with a stepped, cross-shaped temple rising in the middle. The base of the temple is decorated with rows of terracotta plaques showing animals, people and deities. A site museum displays sculpture and objects found during excavation, and the whole site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
blocks: How to get there
Paharpur is in Badalgachhi upazila; reach it by road from Naogaon town or Joypurhat, or by train to Jamalganj station and then a short ride.
Good to know
Go early or late in the day; the site is exposed and hot at midday. Look closely at the terracotta plaques around the temple base.

naogaon-pera-sandesh.desc: Pera sandesh is made by cooking milk and sugar down into a thick kheer, then rolling small portions by hand and pressing them into short logs. The result is dense, fudgy and slightly caramelised in flavour. It is traced to sweet makers in the Kalitala area of Naogaon town, where it was first made as a temple offering. Today it is the sweet visitors are expected to carry home.
blocks: Good to know
It keeps for a few days, so it travels well as a gift.

bhimer-panti.desc: Bhimer Panti is a long block of black stone standing at a tilt in the middle of farmland at Mukundapur–Harogouri in Jahanpur union of Dhamoirhat. It is a protected monument, and local stories link it with Bhima, though no one knows for certain who raised it or when. Old mounds and remains of small temples are scattered around, and a black stone image was found nearby in 1978. Seeing the lonely pillar among the paddy is a strange sight.
blocks: How to get there
From Dhamoirhat take an auto-rickshaw about 10 km south-east towards Jahanpur; it is also reachable from Joypurhat side.
Good to know
Walk along the field ridges and don't trample crops. Ask locals for 'Bhimer Panti'.

raktadaha-beel.desc: Raktadaha Beel spreads across Raninagar in Naogaon and Adamdighi in Bogura, fed by about thirteen canals and channels. Fishing, farming and birds have long depended on it. In January 2025 the upazila administration opened a nature tourism area beside the beel at Hatirpul, with shaded walkways, rest spots, clay pots put up as bird nests and a fish sanctuary. Local media have started calling it the 'Ratargul of the north' for its trees standing in water.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus or CNG from Naogaon to Raninagar, then an auto-rickshaw to Hatirpul.
Good to know
Go in the monsoon or early winter for water and birds; take a boat only with a life jacket.

naogaon-mango.desc: Over the past two decades, farmers in Sapahar, Porsha and Niamatpur have turned dry Barind land into large mango orchards. Amrapali, a small, very sweet variety, is especially common, alongside Langra, Khirsapat and Fazli. In season, Sapahar's mango market is crowded with traders and trucks. Driving through the orchards on the red-soil roads is a pleasure in itself.
blocks: Good to know
Amrapali ripens later than Gopalbhog and Khirsapat; ask what is in season.

glance: Sabbir Hotel and Restaurant, Atapatti, Dharmatala Road, Naogaon town
naogaon-sabbir-biryani.desc: Sabbir Hotel and Restaurant began around 1974 as a small dal, roti and tea shop and turned to biryani and polao in 1980, after one big order of chicken polao drew a crowd. Its khashir (mutton) biryani and murgi polao are what Naogaon people name first when asked where to eat. The menu also has kacchi, rice with fish and meat, bhorta, doi and mihidana laddu. It gets busiest in the afternoon and again around nine at night.
blocks: Good to know
Come before the 9 pm rush if you want a seat.

halud-vihara.desc: Halud Vihara lies about 14.5 km south of Paharpur, in a village locals also call Dwipganj. The main mound is about 65 m by 40 m and 10 m high, with brick walls of what may be a large hall exposed on top and a flight of steps on the eastern slope. Excavations in 1984 and 1993 showed it was a Buddhist site of the same period as Paharpur, and Buddha images, terracotta plaques and coins have been found here. It is on UNESCO's tentative list, yet you will usually have it to yourself.
blocks: How to get there
From Paharpur or Badalgachhi take an auto-rickshaw or CNG south to Halud Vihara village.
Good to know
Visit on the same day as Paharpur. Much brick has been carried off by villagers in the past, so please don't take anything.
